title: Total Processing of a Pair Encoding
statement: For either choice of the program parameter and every bit string $z$, there are a register assignment and an input position such that, on input $z$, the program starting at its scan label with register value $0$ and input position $0$ reaches a halted state with that assignment and position. To describe its appended output, parse $z$ into a first component $a$ and a second component $b$ by reading aligned pairs $00$ and $11$ as bits of $a$ until the separator $01$, with the remaining suffix as $b$; if this parse fails, take both components to be empty. The output appended is the first $|a|$ bits of $b$ when the parameter is true and the suffix of $b$ after its first $|a|$ bits when false, and the run takes at most $5(|z|+1)$ steps; this holds for every output string already printed.
hypotheses_covered: The program parameter is a Boolean choice
The input is an arbitrary bit string $z$
The input position starts at zero
